Hi all,

  duplicate 'row.names' are not allowed

The RecordTableIndividual has rows that are all labeled the same because I want cameras to be independent since some stations have multiple cameras.

rec.db.Tayra <- recordTableIndividual(inDir = "E:/Species_Organized/Tayra" ,
                                     IDfrom = "metadata",
                                     minDeltaTime = 15,
                                     deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord",

Any assistance you can provide would be greatly appreciated!

messages.subject: Does camtrapR work with videos
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm looking at using camtrapR for some camera trap footage in my PhD and was wondering if it handles videos as well as still photos and how well it work.

Thanks!
Kristen Hornbuckle
messages.body_snippet:
Hi everyone,

I'm looking at using camtrapR for some camera trap footage in my PhD and was wondering if it handles videos as well as still photos and how well it work.

Thanks!
Kristen Hornbuckle

messages.subject: Re: Does camtrapR work with videos
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
yes, camtrapR works with videos. See this post <https://groups.google.com/g/camtrapr/c/kM_R8i-0J-U> on the group.
The links  the vignettes given there don't work anymore though, so use these instead:
vignette 1 <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr1.pdf>
vignette 2 <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr2.pdf>

While videos are supported and can be used alongside JPG files, there are some limitations, most notably:
due to non-standardized video metadata you first need to figure out which (if any) metadata tag contains the relevant date/time information
digiKam tags are not saved inside the video file, but only reside in the digiKam database (in contrast, metadata tags are saved inside JPG metadata). This means video tags can be lost when the database breaks or files are moved, and it may be a headache when migrating a digiKam database.
Maybe other users can provide feedback about how well it works. There are also a few more threads here on the group.
Best regards

messages.subject: Detection History by Camera
messages.body_plain:
Hello Juergen,

Is it possible to get detection history for individual cameras (as opposed to by station)? My cameras are on drift fence arrays (2 cameras per array) and I have several instances of one camera from the array being stolen or damaged, but the other one is still operational. Using the station for detection history gives me an "NA" for the whole station even with one camera still operational.

Thanks!

Jen Myers

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Detection History by Camera
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
sounds like it should be addressed via:
camop <- cameraOperation(..., byCamera = FALSE)
detectionHistory(..., includeEffort = TRUE)

That will get rid of the NAs in occasions with incomplete effort.
See this recent thread <https://groups.google.com/g/camtrapr/c/Zh6BJG3_Qk0/m/pL_fllhpAgAJ>. It was about spatialDetectionHistory, but should apply equally to detectionHistory.

The problem with detection histories by camera is that it would likely violate model assumption (independence between stations) if nearby cameras are considered different "stations".
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error in survey report
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
my previous reply was wrong, sorry. cameraOperation() does not have a scaleEffort argument (anymore) and the error message was outdated in the package.

The error about negative effort in the camera operation matrix likely occurred because of some days being in multiple Problem_from/to periods. They are then subtracted from effort multiple times, leading to negative effort.

The current GitHub version should give a better error message with station and days for which the problem occurs,
something like:
Error: Negative effort calculated in StationA__CAM_Camera1 on: Date1, Date2
 Check for overlapping dates in Problem columns

The check is currently for each station individually, not all at once. A bit inconvenient if it affects multiple stations, but at least not misleading anymore.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Confidence interval of Overlap Estimate
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am sorry if this is not the right forum to ask this, but I have a doubt regarding the confidence interval calculated for the overlap estimate, using the package "overlap". But maybe someone here has some insights into this.

I am comparing the activity between two species and I calculated the overlap coefficient Dhat1 and the bootstrap mean of this coefficient so I can calculate the CI. I followed the tutorial from Mike Meredith and Martin Ridout  (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/overlap/vignettes/overlap.pdf). However, for this particular species comparison the bootstrap mean is outside the CI (OverlapEst=0.89, CI= 0.91-0.98). I find this odd, but I have double checked the code and everything seems right. Any idea why this could happen?

>MartenGenet_overlapwinterGrandola <-
>   overlapEst(st_martenwinterGrandola, st_genetwinterGrandola, type="Dhat1")

>## bootstrap to obtain CI
>boot_MartenGenet_GrandolaWinter <-
>    bootstrap(st_martenwinterGrandola, st_genetwinterGrandola, 10000, type="Dhat1")
>### mean delta1 from bootstrap
>MartenGenet_GrandolaBSmean <- round(mean(boot_MartenGenet_GrandolaWinter), 2)
>### CI, basic0
>CI_MartenGenet_GrandolaWinter <-
 >   bootCIlogit(MartenGenet_overlapwinterGrandola, boot_MartenGenet_GrandolaWinter)

Once again, I apologize if this isn't the right place to ask this, but couldn't find a similar forum for the package "overlap". And thank you in advance for any comments.

Cheers,
Ana

  outDir="C:/Users/Home/Documents/2022 Summer Work/MSEC Projects TurkeyGrouse Detection Histories by Camera_200mBuff"
)

Any help would be greatly appreciated as I've run this code many times before without issue.

the expected format does not have dashes, but the actual data do. Did you specify argument CTDateFormat? By default it should be CTDateFormat = "ymd", using the simpler lubridate format and not the base R format (with %). In that case the error message should be different though.

Can you confirm that this still happens with the latest version from Github? If so please share a small subset of the data so I can investigate.  If not please update and try again.

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: Error in multi-species occupancy prediction
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Re: Error in multi-species occupancy prediction
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the "error: cannot allocate vector of size 1.7 Gb" is an out-of-memory error, as you mentioned. Large predictions (especially spatial) with many posterior draws and many species can be extremely memory intensive. There are intermediate objects of dimension: n(sites) x n(species) x n(draws), so we quickly get billions of cells and R objects several Gb large. Fewer posterior draws or smaller prediction raster can help if memory is limited.

The other error: "only 0's may be mixed with negative subscripts" means that R is trying to use negative and positive indices, e.g. x[-1:1], which is not expected behaviour. That is likely a problem related to one of your covariates. Do you have factor covariates in the prediction raster stack? If yes, are they formatted correctly (values are integer numbers indicating the factor level of a cell)? Or do you possibly have negative values (e.g. due to scale()) in the factor covariate of the prediction raster?
Feel free to share the summary() of the raster stack if you're uncertain.

Last point, what exactly do you mean by true occupancy value? Occupancy probability or occupancy status (1/0). Occupancy probability can also be calculated with predict(). Simply provide a data frame with the covariate values at the stations to the function instead of a covariate raster. But be aware that the occupancy probabilities are theoretical, so even with confirmed occupancy at a station (occupancy status = 1) the probability will be <1.

Another possibility, you can return the z matrix (occupancy status for each station & species) from the model. It is not returned by default, but you can include it in the monitored model parameters:

mod.jags <- communityModel(...)
mod.jags@params <- c(mod.jags@params, "z")  # monitor parameter z
fit(...)

Thank you,
Jürgen
